column1: # Clay minerals as sorbents: cation exchange capacity (meq per kg of clay) and N2 (BET) surface area.
# Kaolinite and montmorillonite: the Clay Minerals Society Source Clays KGa-1 (KGa-1b) and SWy-1 (SWy-2), from
# van Olphen and Fripiat (1979, Data Handbook for Clay Materials and Other Non-metallic Minerals, Pergamon) as
# listed by the Source Clays Repository (2.0 and 76.4 meq/100 g; 10.05 and 31.82 m2/g).
# Illite: Na-illite du Puy, CEC 225 meq/kg, the value of the PSI clay sorption model (Marinich, Marques Fernandes,
# Miron and Kulik 2024, ClaySor 2023, Nagra Technical Report NTB 23-05, Table A-1); no N2 area is used here.
# The exchange constants are phreeqc.dat's (sorption.tsv): one set of Gaines-Thomas constants for every clay,
# so the clays differ only in how many sites they carry.
